name: mcp-recipes
description: MCP server that asks Marmiton and the Wikibooks Cookbook at once, merges the answers, and scales quantities in French and English. No API key required.
long_description:
Ask one question and two kitchens answer: Marmiton in French and the Wikibooks Cookbook in English. Search both at once and get one merged list, read either recipe in full, rescale it to any number of people, and put the same dish side by side as each tradition writes it.

The scaling is what this server exists for. Quantities land where a cook can follow them: an egg and a sealed sachet stay whole, a clove halves, a spoonful shrinks into the smaller spoon before it is rounded, and a pinch keeps whatever size a hand gives it while its count is multiplied. One list can hold French lines and English lines at once, and each comes back written the way its own language writes numbers, plurals and measures.

Nothing is converted between measuring systems, no rating is compared across sites, and a site that fails is named as a site that failed rather than folded into an answer as silence.

tools.name: search_recipes
tools.description: Search both recipe sites at once and get one merged list.

query.description: A dish or an ingredient, in any of the languages the sources publish in.

limit_per_source.description: Rows to take from each source, so one source cannot fill the whole list.

sources.description: Sources to ask, by id. Left out, they are all asked, which is the point of this tool. The ids are the ones 'per_source' reports.

fan_out.description: Whether a question may also be sent in shorter wordings derived from it. On, because these indexes answer the words they are handed: a question written as a sentence comes back empty from a corpus holding several of the dish. Turn it off to send exactly the words typed; 'per_source' then names the wordings that were withheld.

tools.name: get_recipe
tools.description: Read one recipe, optionally rescaled to a number of servings.

servings.description: Rescale to this many. Left out, the quantities come back as published.

sections.description: Which parts to return. A full recipe is a lot of text, so this defaults to two.

max_steps.description: Steps to return. The answer says how many more there are.

max_step_chars.description: Characters kept per step. Raise it only if a step was cut mid-sentence.

tools.name: scale_ingredients
tools.description: Scale a list of ingredient lines, in French, English or both.

ingredients.description: The lines as written, one ingredient each, such as '200 g de farine' or '3 eggs'. One line, not a whole recipe.

factor.description: What to multiply by. Give exactly one of: 'factor', or both 'from_servings' and 'to_servings'.

from_servings.description: What the list serves now. Give it with 'to_servings', and without 'factor'.

to_servings.description: What it should serve. Give it with 'from_servings', and without 'factor'.

language.description: 'auto' reads each line on its own, which is what a list holding both languages needs. Name a language to read every line that way.

tools.name: compare_recipes
tools.description: One dish, as each site writes it, side by side.

dish.description: The dish to compare, in any of the languages the sources publish in.

servings.description: Rescale every version to this many, which is what makes the lists comparable.

sections.description: Which parts of each version to return. Several full recipes is a lot of text.

max_step_chars.description: Characters kept per step. Raise it only if a step was cut mid-sentence.
